items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: So he turned to me, he said, 'Why? Are you interested in playing, Stuff?'

ctx.x: And I remember when the rehearsal was over, and Wes and Errol was always laughing and jolly, laughing so much at each other, it was...they had such great rapport and they had such respect for each other. It came out in the music that way, too. They were laughing and talking, and Stuff was putting his bass away. And he came down and I felt like I wanted to ask him a couple of questions.

And I remember asking him, 'What does an instrument like that cost?' So he turned to me, he said, 'Why? Are you interested in playing, Stuff?' And I said, 'No, not particularly. I was just curious.' And so he explained to me how instruments like that are sold, pricewise, what was the going price. Then he wanted to tell me there was a bass in a repair shop down on Ohio St downtown, a guy by the name of...it was Fid's Fiddle Shop. A guy named Fid owned the fiddle shop, and he had it there for sale.

He said he had saw the bass and been looking at it. He really wanted to buy it but he already had two basses and he didn't need another one, but the price was right. He really wanted that bass because it was a good bass. And this went on, and he said, 'Why don't you go and take a look at it because the guy only wants $75 for it.'
